title: Lexicographic Robustness and the Efficiency of Optimal Mechanisms
abstract: arXiv:2604.06105v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The maxmin criterion is commonly used to formalize a mechanism designer's concern for robustness over a set of possible environments. Without substantially restricting this set, however, the criterion may identify a large and economically uninformative collection of mechanisms. This paper proposes a lexicographic, belief-based approach to refining the maxmin criterion and uses it to analyze the efficiency of optimal mechanisms. In canonical screening and auction models, the strongest refinement $\unicode{x2013}$ proper robustness $\unicode{x2013}$ selects ex post efficient mechanisms. By contrast, in a public good provision model, it identifies a unique mechanism whose inefficiency may become severe in large economies.

translated_title: 词典序稳健性与最优机制的效率
translated_abstract: 极大极小准则常被用于形式化机制设计者对一组可能环境的稳健性关注。然而，若不对这组环境施加实质性限制，该准则可能会识别出一个庞大且缺乏经济学信息含量的机制集合。本文提出一种基于信念的词典序方法来细化极大极小准则，并运用该方法分析最优机制的效率。在经典的筛选与拍卖模型中，最强的细化——“适当稳健性”——会选出事后有效的机制。相比之下，在公共物品供给模型中，该方法识别出一个唯一的机制，但其无效率程度在大型经济中可能变得十分严重。
tldr: 本文提出基于信念的词典序方法细化极大极小稳健性准则，证明该细化在筛选与拍卖模型中能选出事后有效的机制，但在公共物品供给模型中所识别的唯一机制在大型经济中可能严重无效率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a lexicographic, belief-based refinement of the maxmin robustness criterion, showing that it selects ex post efficient mechanisms in canonical screening and auction models, while identifying a unique mechanism in public good provision whose inefficiency can become severe in large economies.
